audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Jephthah origin, Ammonite negotiation, war, catastrophic vow, and daughter narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Jephthah's stigmatized maternal origin, expulsion and return, Gilead headship bargain, diplomatic land-history argument, Spirit-before-vow sequence, vow syntax, daughter-centered grief, sacrifice language, and annual commemoration.

verses.restored: Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor, and he was son of a woman who was a sex worker; Gilead fathered Jephthah.

familiar.text: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of an harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah.

modern.text: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor; he was the son of a prostitute, and Gilead was his father.

original.text: וְיִפְתָּ֣ח הַגִּלְעָדִ֗י הָיָה֙ גִּבּ֣וֹר חַ֔יִל וְה֖וּא בֶּן אִשָּׁ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד גִּלְעָ֖ד אֶת יִפְתָּֽח

verses.restored: Gilead's wife bore him sons. When the wife's sons grew, they drove Jephthah out and said to him, You shall not inherit in our father's house, because you are son of another woman.

familiar.text: And Gilead’s wife bare him sons; and his wife’s sons grew up, and they thrust out Jephthah, and said unto him, Thou shalt not inherit in our father’s house; for thou art the son of a strange woman.

modern.text: And Gilead’s wife bore him sons who grew up, drove Jephthah out, and said to him, “You shall have no inheritance in our father’s house, because you are the son of another woman.”

original.text: וַתֵּ֧לֶד אֵֽשֶׁת גִּלְעָ֛ד ל֖וֹ בָּנִ֑ים וַיִּגְדְּל֨וּ בְֽנֵי הָאִשָּׁ֜ה וַיְגָרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת יִפְתָּ֗ח וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֹֽא תִנְחַ֣ל בְּבֵית אָבִ֔ינוּ כִּ֛י בֶּן אִשָּׁ֥ה אַחֶ֖רֶת אָֽתָּה

verses.restored: Jephthah fled from before his brothers and dwelt in land of Tob. Empty/reckless men gathered themselves to Jephthah and went out with him.

familiar.text: Then Jephthah fled from his brethren, and dwelt in the land of Tob: and there were gathered vain men to Jephthah, and went out with him.

modern.text: So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, where worthless men gathered around him and traveled with him.

original.text: וַיִּבְרַ֤ח יִפְתָּח֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י אֶחָ֔יו וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּאֶ֣רֶץ ט֑וֹב וַיִּֽתְלַקְּט֤וּ אֶל יִפְתָּח֙ אֲנָשִׁ֣ים רֵיקִ֔ים וַיֵּצְא֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: After days, sons of Ammon fought with Israel.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in process of time, that the children of Ammon made war against Israel.

modern.text: Some time later, when the Ammonites fought against Israel

original.text: וַיְהִ֖י מִיָּמִ֑ים וַיִּלָּחֲמ֥וּ בְנֵֽי עַמּ֖וֹן עִם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: When sons of Ammon fought with Israel, elders of Gilead went to take Jephthah from land of Tob.

familiar.text: And it was so, that when the children of Ammon made war against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah out of the land of Tob:

modern.text: and made war with them, the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah from the land of Tob.

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁר נִלְחֲמ֥וּ בְנֵֽי עַמּ֖וֹן עִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ זִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד לָקַ֥חַת אֶת יִפְתָּ֖ח מֵאֶ֥רֶץ טֽוֹב

verses.restored: They said to Jephthah, Come, and be for us a commander, so we may fight against sons of Ammon.

familiar.text: And they said unto Jephthah, Come, and be our captain, that we may fight with the children of Ammon.

modern.text: “Come,” they said, “be our commander, so that we can fight against the Ammonites.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְיִפְתָּ֔ח לְכָ֕ה וְהָיִ֥יתָה לָּ֖נוּ לְקָצִ֑ין וְנִֽלָּחֲמָ֖ה בִּבְנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

verses.restored: Jephthah said to elders of Gilead, Did you not hate me and drive me from my father's house? Why have you come to me now, when distress is upon you?

familiar.text: And Jephthah said unto the elders of Gilead, Did not ye hate me, and expel me out of my father’s house? and why are ye come unto me now when ye are in distress?

modern.text: Jephthah replied to the elders of Gilead, “Did you not hate me and expel me from my father’s house? Why then have you come to me now, when you are in distress?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִפְתָּח֙ לְזִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד הֲלֹ֤א אַתֶּם֙ שְׂנֵאתֶ֣ם אוֹתִ֔י וַתְּגָרְשׁ֖וּנִי מִבֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וּמַדּ֜וּעַ בָּאתֶ֤ם אֵלַי֙ עַ֔תָּה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צַ֥ר לָכֶֽם

verses.restored: Elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, Therefore now we have returned to you: you shall go with us and fight against sons of Ammon, and you shall be head for us, for all inhabitants of Gilead.

familiar.text: And the elders of Gilead said unto Jephthah, Therefore we turn again to thee now, that thou mayest go with us, and fight against the children of Ammon, and be our head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.

modern.text: They answered Jephthah, “This is why we now turn to you, that you may go with us, fight the Ammonites, and become leader over all of us who live in Gilead.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ זִקְנֵ֨י גִלְעָ֜ד אֶל יִפְתָּ֗ח לָכֵן֙ עַתָּה֙ שַׁ֣בְנוּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ֣ עִמָּ֔נוּ וְנִלְחַמְתָּ֖ בִּבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וְהָיִ֤יתָ לָּ֨נוּ֙ לְרֹ֔אשׁ לְכֹ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י גִלְעָֽד

verses.restored: Jephthah said to elders of Gilead, If you bring me back to fight against sons of Ammon, and YHWH gives them before me, I shall be your head.

familiar.text: And Jephthah said unto the elders of Gilead, If ye bring me home again to fight against the children of Ammon, and the LORD deliver them before me, shall I be your head?

modern.text: But Jephthah asked them, “If you take me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them to me, will I really be your leader?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִפְתָּ֜ח אֶל זִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֗ד אִם מְשִׁיבִ֨ים אַתֶּ֤ם אוֹתִי֙ לְהִלָּחֵם֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וְנָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אוֹתָ֖ם לְפָנָ֑י אָנֹכִ֕י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לְרֹֽאשׁ

verses.restored: Elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, YHWH shall be hearer/witness between us if we do not do according to your word.

familiar.text: And the elders of Gilead said unto Jephthah, The LORD be witness between us, if we do not so according to thy words.

modern.text: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “The LORD is our witness if we do not do as you say.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ זִקְנֵֽי גִלְעָ֖ד אֶל יִפְתָּ֑ח יְהוָ֗ה יִהְיֶ֤ה שֹׁמֵ֨עַ֙ בֵּֽינוֹתֵ֔ינוּ אִם לֹ֥א כִדְבָרְךָ֖ כֵּ֥ן נַעֲשֶֽׂה

verses.restored: Jephthah went with elders of Gilead, and the people set him over them as head and commander. Jephthah spoke all his words before YHWH at Mizpah.

familiar.text: Then Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and captain over them: and Jephthah uttered all his words before the LORD in Mizpeh.

modern.text: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him their leader and commander. And Jephthah repeated all his terms in the presence of the LORD at Mizpah.

original.text: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ יִפְתָּח֙ עִם זִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד וַיָּשִׂ֨ימוּ הָעָ֥ם אוֹת֛וֹ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לְרֹ֣אשׁ וּלְקָצִ֑ין וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יִפְתָּ֧ח אֶת כָּל דְּבָרָ֛יו לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בַּמִּצְפָּֽה

verses.restored: Jephthah sent messengers to king of sons of Ammon, saying, What is there between me and you, that you have come against me to fight in my land?

familiar.text: And Jephthah sent messengers unto the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What hast thou to do with me, that thou art come against me to fight in my land?

modern.text: Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, saying, “What do you have against me that you have come to fight against my land?”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִפְתָּח֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל מֶ֥לֶךְ בְּנֵֽי עַמּ֖וֹן לֵאמֹ֑ר מַה לִּ֣י וָלָ֔ךְ כִּֽי בָ֥אתָ אֵלַ֖י לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם בְּאַרְצִֽי

verses.restored: King of sons of Ammon said to Jephthah's messengers, Because Israel took my land when it came up from Egypt, from Arnon to Jabbok and to Jordan; now return them in peace.

familiar.text: And the king of the children of Ammon answered unto the messengers of Jephthah, Because Israel took away my land, when they came up out of Egypt, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and unto Jordan: now therefore restore those lands again peaceably.

modern.text: The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah’s messengers, “When Israel came up out of Egypt, they seized my land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and all the way to the Jordan. Now, therefore, restore it peaceably.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בְּנֵי עַמּ֜וֹן אֶל מַלְאֲכֵ֣י יִפְתָּ֗ח כִּֽי לָקַ֨ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶת אַרְצִי֙ בַּעֲלוֹת֣וֹ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם מֵאַרְנ֥וֹן וְעַד הַיַּבֹּ֖ק וְעַד הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְעַתָּ֕ה הָשִׁ֥יבָה אֶתְהֶ֖ן בְּשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Jephthah again sent messengers to king of sons of Ammon.

familiar.text: And Jephthah sent messengers again unto the king of the children of Ammon:

modern.text: Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites

original.text: וַיּ֥וֹסֶף ע֖וֹד יִפְתָּ֑ח וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

verses.restored: He said to him, Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take land of Moab or land of sons of Ammon.

familiar.text: And said unto him, Thus saith Jephthah, Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon:

modern.text: to tell him, “This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take away the land of Moab or of the Ammonites.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יִפְתָּ֑ח לֹֽא לָקַ֤ח יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת אֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב וְאֶת אֶ֖רֶץ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

verses.restored: For when they came up from Egypt, Israel walked in wilderness as far as Sea of Reeds and came to Kadesh.

familiar.text: But when Israel came up from Egypt, and walked through the wilderness unto the Red sea, and came to Kadesh;

modern.text: But when Israel came up out of Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.

original.text: כִּ֖י בַּעֲלוֹתָ֣ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ עַד יַם ס֔וּף וַיָּבֹ֖א קָדֵֽשָׁה

verses.restored: Israel sent messengers to king of Edom, saying, Please let me pass through your land, but king of Edom did not listen. They also sent to king of Moab, but he was unwilling, so Israel stayed at Kadesh.

familiar.text: Then Israel sent messengers unto the king of Edom, saying, Let me, I pray thee, pass through thy land: but the king of Edom would not hearken thereto. And in like manner they sent unto the king of Moab: but he would not consent: and Israel abode in Kadesh.

modern.text: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let us pass through your land,’ but the king of Edom would not listen. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel stayed in Kadesh.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מַלְאָכִ֣ים אֶל מֶלֶךְ֩ אֱד֨וֹם לֵאמֹ֜ר אֶעְבְּרָה נָּ֣א בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַע֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֱד֔וֹם וְגַ֨ם אֶל מֶ֧לֶךְ מוֹאָ֛ב שָׁלַ֖ח וְלֹ֣א אָבָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּקָדֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: They walked in wilderness, went around land of Edom and land of Moab, came from east of sun toward land of Moab, and camped across Arnon. They did not enter border of Moab, because Arnon was border of Moab.

familiar.text: Then they went along through the wilderness, and compassed the land of Edom, and the land of Moab, and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and pitched on the other side of Arnon, but came not within the border of Moab: for Arnon was the border of Moab.

modern.text: Then Israel traveled through the wilderness and bypassed the lands of Edom and Moab. They came to the east side of the land of Moab and camped on the other side of the Arnon. But they did not enter the territory of Moab, since the Arnon was its border.

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר וַיָּ֜סָב אֶת אֶ֤רֶץ אֱדוֹם֙ וְאֶת אֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּבֹ֤א מִמִּזְרַח שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ לְאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּן בְּעֵ֣בֶר אַרְנ֑וֹן וְלֹא בָ֨אוּ֙ בִּגְב֣וּל מוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֥י אַרְנ֖וֹן גְּב֥וּל מוֹאָֽב

verses.restored: Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of Amorite, king of Heshbon. Israel said to him, Please let us pass through your land to my place.

familiar.text: And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon; and Israel said unto him, Let us pass, we pray thee, through thy land into my place.

modern.text: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land into our own place.’

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל סִיח֥וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נַעְבְּרָה נָּ֥א בְאַרְצְךָ֖ עַד מְקוֹמִֽי

verses.restored: But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his border. Sihon gathered all his people, camped at Jahaz, and fought with Israel.

familiar.text: But Sihon trusted not Israel to pass through his coast: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and pitched in Jahaz, and fought against Israel.

modern.text: But Sihon would not trust Israel to pass through his territory. So he gathered all his people, encamped in Jahaz, and fought with Israel.

original.text: וְלֹא הֶאֱמִ֨ין סִיח֤וֹן אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עֲבֹ֣ר בִּגְבֻל֔וֹ וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף סִיחוֹן֙ אֶת כָּל עַמּ֔וֹ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּיָ֑הְצָה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם עִם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: YHWH, Divine of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into hand of Israel, and they struck them. Israel possessed all land of Amorite inhabiting that land.

familiar.text: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country.

modern.text: Then the LORD, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, who defeated them. So Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that country,

original.text: וַ֠יִּתֵּן יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת סִיח֧וֹן וְאֶת כָּל עַמּ֛וֹ בְּיַ֥ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיַּכּ֑וּם וַיִּירַשׁ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֚ת כָּל אֶ֣רֶץ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י יוֹשֵׁ֖ב הָאָ֥רֶץ הַהִֽיא

verses.restored: They possessed all border of Amorite, from Arnon to Jabbok and from wilderness to Jordan.

familiar.text: And they possessed all the coasts of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan.

modern.text: seizing all the land from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.

original.text: וַיִּ֣ירְשׁ֔וּ אֵ֖ת כָּל גְּב֣וּל הָאֱמֹרִ֑י מֵֽאַרְנוֹן֙ וְעַד הַיַּבֹּ֔ק וּמִן הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְעַד הַיַּרְדֵּֽן

verses.restored: And now YHWH, Divine of Israel, has dispossessed Amorite from before his people Israel; and you would possess it?

familiar.text: So now the LORD God of Israel hath dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and shouldest thou possess it?

modern.text: Now since the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites from before His people Israel, should you now possess it?

original.text: וְעַתָּ֞ה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הוֹרִישׁ֙ אֶת הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י מִפְּנֵ֖י עַמּ֣וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּירָשֶֽׁנּוּ

verses.restored: Will you not possess whatever Chemosh your god causes you to possess? And whatever YHWH our Divine has dispossessed from before us, that we will possess.

translation_notes: Verse 1 preserves the stigmatizing label zonah for Jephthah's mother. Her occupation or social classification does not diminish her humanity or make Jephthah morally defective.
Jephthah is expelled from inheritance by his brothers and later recruited by the same leadership during crisis; the headship bargain exposes opportunistic use of an outcast person.

Jephthah first attempts extended diplomacy. His historical argument distinguishes Ammonite and Moabite claims, though verse 24's reference to Chemosh as Ammon's god is historically and textually difficult.
The Spirit of YHWH comes upon Jephthah in verse 29 before he makes the vow. The vow is not required to secure Divine presence or victory.

Verses 30-31 use explicit vow and ascending-offering language. Attempts to make the vow harmless by default are not secure; the narrative must be read under Torah's rejection of child sacrifice and its provisions for evaluating or redeeming vows.
Jephthah's statement that he cannot turn back is his claim, not a Divine command. A vow cannot create a righteous duty to abuse or kill another person.
Verse 35 shifts blame onto the daughter for a danger created entirely by Jephthah. The translation preserves the accusation so its victim-blaming can be recognized and rejected.

The daughter is never named, but she speaks, requests time, gathers companions, and becomes the center of a women's memorial practice. Her consent cannot be inferred from speech produced inside paternal, military, religious, and social coercion.
Virginity language marks the loss of her own future, relationships, descendants, and bodily autonomy; it does not make sexual inexperience a superior spiritual state.
Verse 39's wording, 'he did to her his vow,' remains terse and horrifying. The source layer should not erase the likely death, while noting the history of alternative dedication readings.
Letannot in verse 40 may carry senses such as recount, commemorate, praise, or lament. The annual gathering preserves the daughter's memory rather than celebrating Jephthah.
safety_note: Maximum safeguard: Jephthah's vow is catastrophic, abusive, and incompatible with any ethic that protects children. Do not praise it as faith, obedience, sacrifice, masculine honor, or spiritual courage. Do not blame his daughter, infer free consent, demand that victims honor another person's vow, or use this chapter to justify child sacrifice, self-sacrifice, coercive promises, honor violence, forced celibacy, or religious control. The women who remember her provide the chapter's clearest counter-memory.
